supporting_observations.claim: At 13:42:41 UTC, a Windows security event recorded hana.ito being added to the RIVERBEND Billing-Share group by dev.sharma.
The group-change event used logon ID 0x1307103b, which was associated shortly beforehand with a Kerberos network logon for dev.sharma to DC-RB-01 from IP 10.60.10.23 and a privileged-logon event.

The source IP is the address used by WS-DSHARMA-01 for an RDP connection to DC-RB-01, consistent with the stated practice that server administration is performed from that workstation. The RDP session was recorded after the group-change event, so the evidence does not establish that it caused the change.
The changed membership—hana.ito added to Billing-Share—matches the access change described in the organization's change calendar for that afternoon.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records attribute the group change to dev.sharma and a logon ID, but do not identify the process, tool, or user interface that performed the change.
The evidence does not include the change ticket or other approval record needed to verify that the required ticket existed.
The supplied logs cover a limited time window and do not establish whether there was other relevant activity outside it.
claims_not_established: Whether a ticket was opened and approved for hana.ito's Billing-Share access.
Whether dev.sharma personally initiated the group change or whether the account or session was being used by another party.
Whether the change was performed interactively or through another mechanism.
unrelated_findings: WS-DSHARMA-01's OpenSSH client connected to PROXY-RB-01 on TCP port 22. The inventory identifies PROXY-RB-01 as an explicit web proxy and says no remote-access tools are approved; these records show a connection attempt but do not establish that a remote shell was successfully used. Review separately. (S28-00004, S28-00007)

Explorer UserAssist registry records on WS-HITO-01 contain ROT13-encoded paths corresponding to PowerShell and mstsc.exe. These records suggest those applications were launched under hana.ito, but do not provide command lines or establish what they did. Review separately. (S28-00043, S28-00054)
